```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(cache = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

First let's load the WHO dataset from the tidyr package.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

#View(tidyr::who)
```

# Step 1: gather
Here we drop redundant columns regarding country (iso2, iso3) and transform the table to be more long than wide.

```{r}
who1 <- who %>%
  pivot_longer(!(country:year), names_to = "cases", values_to = "counts", values_drop_na = TRUE)

who1
```

# Step 2: replace

```{r}
who2 <- who1 %>% 
  mutate(key = stringr::str_replace(cases, "newrel", "new_rel"))

slice(who2, 242:246)
```
# Step 3: separate

Let's start with separating the cases column with 3 different variables "new", "type" and "sexage".

```{r}
who3 <- who2 %>% 
  separate(key, into = c("new", "type", "sexage"), sep = "_")
who3
```
Now separate seaxage into "sex" and "age".

```{r}
who4 <- who3 %>% 
  separate(sexage, into = c("sex", "age"), sep = 1)
who4
```
Now let's separate age into "age_low" and "age_high".

```{r}
who5 <- who4 %>% 
  mutate(age = stringr::str_replace(age, "014", "0014")) %>%
  mutate(age = stringr::str_replace(age, "65", "65100")) %>%
  separate(age, into = c("age_low", "age_high"), sep = 2)
who5
```

```{r}
# check that new is constant
who5 %>% count(new)

# drop redundant columns
who6 <- who5 %>% 
  select(-new, -iso2, -iso3)
who6
```


# As a whole complete pipe

This is the whole source just rewritten with the pipe operator (|>)
```{r}
who |>
  pivot_longer(!(country:year), names_to = "cases", values_to = "counts", values_drop_na = TRUE) |>
  mutate(key = stringr::str_replace(cases, "newrel", "new_rel")) |>
  separate(key, into = c("new", "type", "sexage"), sep = "_") |>
  separate(sexage, into = c("sex", "age"), sep = 1) |>
  mutate(age = stringr::str_replace(age, "014", "0014")) |>
  mutate(age = stringr::str_replace(age, "65", "65100")) |>
  separate(age, into = c("age_low", "age_high"), sep = 2) |>
  select(-new, -iso2, -iso3)
```
